title: Example Course
sources: courses/example/sources/binary-search-notes.md: short original notes written for this example; the only reading in the course.
notes: A one-unit course that shows the format. Replace it with your own courses (see skills/course/SKILL.md), or keep it to try a session end to end.

concepts.claim: Binary search is correct because it keeps an interval that must contain the target if it is present, and every step preserves that.
Each step at least halves the interval, so the worst case is floor(log2 n) + 1 steps.
the learner can write the half-open version (lo < hi; lo = mid + 1; hi = mid) without mixing it with the closed-interval updates.
Computing mid as lo + (hi - lo) / 2 avoids the integer overflow that (lo + hi) / 2 can cause.
The lower-bound variant returns the first index not less than the target, which answers membership, insertion position and counting with one routine.
the learner can recognize a problem as a search for the boundary of a monotone predicate and binary-search over the answer.
